title: smime-tree: SignerResult.error field carries Option<String> instead of structured error
description:
Why this exists: smime_tree/src/error.rs defines SignerResult with a field error: Option<String>. When verification of a single signer fails, the error is stored as a plain string rather than a structured variant.

What goes wrong: a caller that wants to distinguish 'signature cryptographically invalid' from 'certificate expired' from 'chain validation failed' must parse the string — which is fragile, not type-safe, and will break silently if the string format changes. The rest of SmimeError uses typed variants with fields; using Option<String> here is an inconsistency that forces callers into string-matching.

Location: smime-tree/src/error.rs, SignerResult::error field.

Fix: change error: Option<String> to error: Option<SmimeError> (or a dedicated SignerError enum if that has better semver properties). Update all construction sites.
close_reason: SignerResult.error is Option<String> because signer failures come from diverse sources (DER, chain validation, signature). Converting to a structured type would require a new per-signer error enum. The string carries the Display output which is sufficient for logging. P2 refactoring.
